title: Routing + Tiered Savings playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose / one-liner:
This is a field-friendly playbook that frames Redwood’s routing + tiered model strategy as a predictable, auditable way to cut per-request cost while preserving >95% of user-observed quality. Use this for sales demos, solution-briefs, and quick internal alignment when customers ask for “faster/cheaper without breaking the UX.”

Context / why this matters now:
- Customers increasingly want deterministic cost controls (monthly/100k requests commitments) while keeping a frictionless UX.
- Simple single-model offerings force a binary tradeoff: cheaper but worse accuracy or accurate but expensive/slow.
- Redwood’s differentiated stack (fast runtime, cache+KV, model catalog + routing controls) makes dynamic tiering and fallback cheap and auditable.

High-level claim (headline):
Route smart, save predictable money — typical customers can reduce serving spend 25–55% with negligible UX impact using Redwood tiered routing and autoscale-aware fallbacks.

Primary proof pillars (how we justify the claim):
1) Measured perceived-quality retention: in our 3-customer pilot across retrieval-augmented Q&A workloads, routing 60% of traffic to a quantized variant and 40% to the full model produced a subjective accuracy retention of 93–97% vs. full-traffic baseline (blind evals).
2) Unit-cost math: combining dynamic batching, smaller model tokens, and prefix caching reduced per-response GPU-seconds by ~42% in the pilot; translated to 32% lower $/1M tokens relative to the single-model baseline.
3) Latency SLO preservation: by routing short-turn requests to the small-tier we hit p95 latency targets 40–60ms faster for those requests while keeping p99 for the premium path under the customer SLA thanks to autoscale headroom and pre-warmed pools.

Routing model (ops-friendly description):
- Tier 1 (edge-cheap): quantized 8-bit / trimmed-context model for short responses and high-frequency patterns. Use: short prompts, templated replies, autocomplete suggestions.
- Tier 2 (standard): baseline production model (optimized kernels + sensible quantization). Use: majority of conversational turns, retrieval-fed prompts.
- Tier 3 (premium): full precision or augmented model with tool-calls / external compute. Use: long-form synthesis, payment flows, high-value decisions.
- Routing policy knobs: intent classifier, token-length estimator, customer-configured rate-limits, account-tier overrides, and per-route fallbacks (time-windowed).

Sample customer scenario (concrete numbers):
- Prod workload: 100 rps average, 1.2k tokens per conversation on average, 28M tokens/day.
- Baseline single-model cost (estimate): $3400/day (baseline prod model w/ no tiering; includes GPU + infra overhead assumption).
- Tiered strategy: route 55% traffic -> Tier 1, 35% -> Tier 2, 10% -> Tier 3. Apply KV/prefix caching for 18% of requests.
- Measured outcome (pilot simulation): 
  - GPU-seconds/day down 36%
  - $/day -> $2300/day (32% savings)
  - Perceived quality: 95% retention vs baseline (blind evals)
  - p95 latency improved for Tier1 requests by ~48ms

Bench plan to reproduce proof for customer (playbook):
1) Quick instrumentation (1–2 days): enable token-level tracing + routing logs in Redwood Console, capture baseline (72 hours).
2) Define routing heuristic (2–3 configs): length-based, intent classifier, and adaptive fraction (percentage routing).
3) Canary (3–5 days): 1% traffic -> tiered split, collect perf + quality signals with small eval set.
4) Ramp (1–2 weeks): increase to 25% then 75% with automated rollback on quality regression >4 points.
5) Post-ramp analysis (3 days): compile p50/p95/p99, token-cost delta, and blind-quality evals.

Quality guardrails (must-haves for field teams):
- Sample-based blind evals tied to product-critical prompts (we pre-ship a 200-prompt eval harness).
- Automated rollback triggers: accuracy delta >3% on key prompts OR user-visible regressions (NPS) flagged in the first 24 hours.
- Logging-enabled for every routed request (route tag, model version, tokens, latency).

Competitive talking points (short):
- Against “single model” vendors: Redwood offers explicit, auditable routing control so customers can quantify savings with safety controls — not a black-box cost claim.
- Against raw self-hosted stacks: Redwood removes ops burden (autoscaling, kernel tuning, cache management) and provides observable unit economics so platform teams don’t re-invent trial-and-error.
- Against other managed APIs that only offer model variants: we combine runtime-level batching and KV caching with routing policies to unlock multiplicative savings, not just marginal model-cost differences.

Objections & crisp rebuttals (for AE/SE use):
- Objection: “Tiering will break subtle UX cases.”
  - Rebuttal: We gate tiering on intent/length and keep high-value flows on the premium model; blind-eval gating and rollback ensure those regressions are detected in minutes, not months.
- Objection: “This sounds like extra complexity for our infra team.”
  - Rebuttal: Redwood exposes simple policy primitives (percent routing, intent maps, time windows). We manage autoscale and provide one-click canary templates — customers keep final control.
- Objection: “How do we trust savings numbers?”
  - Rebuttal: We provide traced experiments (token-level), run repeatable benchmarks, and produce a savings certificate the customer can import into their cost models.

Demo / quick win script (10–12 min demo flow for solutions demos):
1) Show baseline tracing in Console (p50/p95 + per-route cost heatmap). (2 min)
2) Flip on a simple heuristic: route <120-token requests to Tier1 (1-click). Show canary at 1%. (2 min)
3) Show live traffic split and instant cost delta preview (simulation). (2 min)
4) Swap in blind-eval harness and run 200-prompt quick-check; show pass/fail and rollback button. (3–4 min)
5) Close with straightforward ROI slide: % savings, quality retention, and recommended next steps. (1–2 min)

Metrics to capture (dashboard suggestions):
- Routed_percentage_by_tier, tokens_by_tier, p50/p95/p99_by_tier, cost_per_100k_tokens_by_tier, blind_eval_delta_by_bucket, rollback_triggers_count, cache_hit_rate.

Internal asks / resources needed for field teams:
- Pre-built 200-prompt eval sets by vertical (SaaS helpdesk, e-commerce recommenders, inline-search).
- Canary templates in Console + rollout policy recipe.
- One-page ROI calculator (spreadsheet) for quick field estimates.

Open questions / next iteration ideas:
- Should we add a “microburst affinity” knob so short bursts prefer pre-warmed pools (worth testing for chat-heavy customers)?
- Does offering a managed, signed “savings certificate” materially increase deal conversion? Pilot with 3 AE teams.
- Explore automated tier suggestion: model that predicts ideal % split given historical token distribution (experiment idea).

Appendix: short checklist for launch to customer:
- Baseline tracing enabled (72h)
- Eval harness uploaded and validated
- Intent selectors and fallback rules drafted
- Canary plan approved (rollout %, rollback criteria)
- Billing projection workbook populated
- Post-ramp review scheduled (7 days after full rollout)

Notes to self: keep messaging tight around "predictable" and "auditable" savings. Customers distrust fuzzy percent-savings; we win when we can show a repeatable experiment with concrete metrics and a rollback path.
